title: Stable Process Limits and Uniform Bands for Quantile Treatment Effects under Weak Overlap
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: tier incremental < floor field; score ceiling 5.7 < 7.4, with inverse-localization and feasible-normalization gaps unresolved.
gap_reasons: The proof does not construct the required unbounded monotone localization with centered limit zero or verify its endpoint conditions.
Local J1 convergence on T^+ is not itself Whitt's D_u, y(0)=0 hypothesis; supply the monotone extension and prove it leaves target inverses unchanged.
The headline general-covariate band is not an implementable inference procedure: it requires the law-defined q_n^{rv}=min_a(n/h_{a,n}), while h_{a,n} is chosen from the unknown selected-weight tail.
The inverse/Taylor route uses only a positive continuous density (so Q' is uniformly continuous); no reproduced step uses f_a' or the claimed C^1 density.
Atomlessness supplies disjoint jumps, while the displayed uniform witness verifies nondegeneracy directly.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery constructed a marked weighted-CDF process argument and extended the quadratic benchmark to a regularly varying oracle class, with source attestations for Whitt's inverse and M1 addition theorems and the finite-dimensional comparator. The math panel still found that the note did not verify the localization and endpoint hypotheses needed to apply the inverse theorem, and the decision panel found the general band uses an unavailable law-defined normalization. D0.5 graded the delivered package incremental (score ceiling 5.7 against the field threshold 7.4); no Lean formalization was reached, and the whole-curve and band headlines are not established by this banked artifact.
tldr: Selected inverse weights with arm-specific regularly varying indices \(\gamma_a\in(1,2)\) generate marked stable distribution-function bridges. For atomless endpoint mark laws, the paper proves their joint threshold-indexed law at rates \(r_{a,n}=n/h_{a,n}\), maps the arm CDF limits to treated and control quantile-error paths in product \(M_1\), and derives the scalar \(M_1\) QTE limit at \(q_n=\min_a r_{a,n}\), including balanced and both one-arm-dominant regimes. Atomic endpoint marks are excluded; obtaining a joint path representation, conditional subset law, and simultaneous band when transformed atomic jump times coincide remains open. Without-replacement \(m_n\)-out-of-\(n\) subsets consistently estimate the proved conditional path law and calibrate whole-curve bands, with exact coverage at a regular critical quantile and fixed-padding conservative coverage otherwise. The fitted quadratic offset-logistic model remains an explicit feasible \(\gamma_0=\gamma_1=3/2\) corollary, and its independent-uniform witness rules out \(J_1\).
gap: The closest weak-overlap QTE paper derives finite-dimensional stable laws and checks only one conditional resampling ingredient. Gaussian whole-curve QTE theory does not apply when the selected inverse weights have infinite variance.
fill: The project supplies that process theorem for an analytically transparent two-boundary propensity, proves feasible fitted-propensity transfer, establishes conditional product-\(M_1\) subsampling, and separates exact critical-quantile coverage from an honest padded conservative rule.
